turns.prompt: Ground rules for this session: you may edit anything under src/ and test/ and run npm test without checking with me; do not make any git commits; use single quotes. First, add capitalize(str) to src/str.js with a test.
turns.final:
Added `capitalize(str)` to `src/str.js:7` plus a test in `test/str.test.js:12`. Both tests pass.

One design note: `capitalize` uses `str[0]`, which splits on UTF-16 code units, so astral-plane characters (emoji, some CJK extensions) would be mangled. For ASCII-ish input it's fine; say the word if you want it to iterate by code point instead.

turns.prompt: Now add a reverse(str) helper the same way.
turns.final:
Added `reverse(str)` to `src/str.js:12` with a test in `test/str.test.js:20`. All three tests pass.

I used `[...str]` rather than `str.split('')` — spread iterates by code point, so surrogate pairs survive intact instead of being split into mojibake. It still reverses combining marks and ZWJ emoji sequences incorrectly (`'e\u0301'` → the accent lands on nothing); correct grapheme handling needs `Intl.Segmenter`. Worth doing only if this ever sees non-ASCII input.

turns.final:
Added `countWords(str)` to `src/str.js:16` with a test in `test/str.test.js:27`. All four tests pass.

Implementation note: it matches `/\S+/g` rather than splitting on whitespace, which avoids the `''.split(/\s+/)` → `['']` trap that would report 1 word for an empty string. Whitespace-only input correctly returns 0.

The definition it encodes is "runs of non-whitespace," so `don't` is one word but `foo--bar` is also one, and `hello,world` (no space) counts as one. That's the usual `wc -w` behavior; if you need punctuation-aware splitting, that's a different function.
